You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

name: arc-bridge-between-markers
description: Use for ARC grids where same-color markers appear in rows/columns and gaps may be bridged. Infer and apply straight-line fills from demonstrations.
---

# ARC: bridge gaps between aligned markers

Use when a demo shows a sparse marker color in a background grid and cells between aligned markers change to a third color.

## Rule observed
For each row and each column independently, identify cells of the marker color. For any pair of marker cells sharing that row or column, recolor background cells strictly between the endpoints to the demonstrated bridge color. Preserve marker cells and all other cells. Equivalently, fill the entire interval from the minimum to maximum marker coordinate in each row/column that contains at least two markers. Apply all horizontal and vertical fills simultaneously; overlapping fills are still the bridge color.

A demonstrated instance used marker 6, background 8, bridge 3; another used marker 2, background 5, bridge 3. Treat colors as task-specific and confirm the pattern against demos before applying.

## Verification
- Preserve grid dimensions and marker locations.
- Change only background cells lying between at least two same-color markers in one row or column.
- Do not extrapolate beyond the outermost markers.
- If demos show a different endpoint/pairing rule, prioritize the demonstrations over this heuristic.",
